Name: subliminal_conditional_gating
Title: Two Directions, One Backdoor: Are Subliminally-Installed Conditional Traits a Gated Steering Vector, and Does Gating Make Them Stealthier Yet Stickier?
Short Hypothesis: A trait installed subliminally under a trigger condition (only active when a trigger token/context is present) is mechanistically factorizable into two dissociable early-layer directions: a trigger-detection direction and an always-latent payload steering direction that is gated by it. This decomposition predicts a counterintuitive safety asymmetry: because the payload direction only fires in the presence of the trigger, trigger-gating shields the subliminal trait from the exact perturbations (prompt paraphrasing, benign safety fine-tuning) that erase ungated subliminal traits during ordinary evaluation, making conditional subliminal traits simultaneously stealthier (invisible without the trigger) AND stickier (surviving repairs that erase ungated versions) than both ungated subliminal traits and overtly-installed backdoors. Novelty is threefold and separable: a FINDING (conditional subliminal traits are simultaneously stealthier and stickier than both ungated subliminal traits and overt backdoors), a MECHANISM (the conditional trait is not one direction but a gated pair -- a trigger-detection direction and a normally-dormant payload direction), and a SETTING/RISK (the payload's dormancy, not its content, is what shields it from the data-level and benign-safety repairs auditors rely on).
Related Work: Cloud et al. (2025) established subliminal learning as always-on trait transfer requiring matched base models. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized transmission to rare divergence tokens and early layers and, crucially, found ungated subliminal traits are FRAGILE - paraphrasing usually suppresses them. Phantom Transfer (2026) is the closest prior work: it modifies subliminal learning to plant password-triggered behaviors that beat data-level defenses (including full paraphrasing of the dataset) and connects to steering vectors - but it is an ATTACK demonstration; it does not mechanistically decompose the conditional trait into separable trigger and payload directions, nor does it test whether trigger-gating changes the erasability/fragility of the underlying subliminal trait relative to its ungated counterpart. Overt-poisoning backdoor work (BadEdit 2024, Concept-ROT 2024, BrieFool/conditional backdoors 2025) shows backdoors resist safety tuning but installs them via explicit trigger-response pairs, not through content-free number data. Re-Emergent Misalignment (2025) shows ungated traits ride a shared erasable direction. No prior work asks (a) whether a subliminally-installed conditional trait is a single payload steering direction gated by a separate trigger-detection direction, or (b) whether gating dissociates the known fragility of subliminal traits from their erasability under safety repair. We turn Phantom Transfer's attack into a mechanistic dissociation and a safety-boundary claim, distinct from all prior attack-only or ungated work. Delta table (prose form), comparing this work against the closest families on four axes -- conditionality, mechanistic factorization into separable directions, causal intervention that dissociates trigger from payload, and a repair-resistance claim tied to dormancy: Phantom Transfer (2026) has conditionality and beats data-level defenses but offers no factorization, no dissociating intervention, and no dormancy-based repair-resistance claim; steering-vector distillation work has a single always-on direction (no conditionality, no gating); shared-latent-direction backdoor papers (BadEdit, Concept-ROT, BrieFool) have conditionality and repair-resistance but install via overt trigger-response pairs and never separate a detector from a gated payload learned through content-free numbers. Two-direction factorization is NOT the trivial 'detector + policy' decomposition of any conditional behavior: the non-trivial, falsifiable claims are (i) the payload direction is present and measurable even when the trigger is absent (a latent, dormant object), and (ii) the SAME payload direction, once extracted, transfers across different triggers -- neither of which a generic detector-gates-policy description predicts. Rival accounts we explicitly discriminate against: (R1) a single steering vector with a context-dependent readout, (R2) an entangled trigger+payload subspace, and (R3) a distributed multi-layer circuit with no low-dimensional payload. Experiment 7 gives a prediction unique to the two-direction account that R1-R3 fail.
Abstract: Subliminal learning transmits behavioral traits through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences, and prior work reports that these traits are FRAGILE: paraphrasing the data or lightly fine-tuning usually erases them. A recent attack (Phantom Transfer) shows that trigger-conditioned versions of such traits can nonetheless be planted and survive data-level defenses. We ask the mechanistic question this leaves open: what IS a subliminally-installed conditional trait? We hypothesize it factorizes into two dissociable early-layer directions - a trigger-detection direction that senses the activating condition and a normally-dormant payload steering direction that is gated by it - and that this gating produces a safety-relevant asymmetry: the payload only fires when the trigger is present, so conditional subliminal traits are shielded from the paraphrasing and benign safety fine-tuning that erase their ungated counterparts, making them both stealthier and stickier. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA fine-tuning, we implant matched ungated and trigger-gated subliminal traits (a benign preference and a safety-relevant trait) through rigorously filtered number/code data, verify triggered vs. untriggered behavior, and (1) locate candidate trigger-detection and payload directions via difference-in-means/probing at early layers; (2) causally dissociate them - patch the trigger direction to fire the payload without the trigger, and ablate the payload direction to disarm the trait while leaving trigger detection intact - reporting sign, dose-response, and specificity; and (3) compare fragility/stickiness of gated vs. ungated vs. overtly-installed traits under paraphrasing and benign safety fine-tuning. Our results reframe conditional subliminal backdoors as a gated two-direction object and quantify a stealth-plus-durability safety hole. So what: if H2 holds, two widely-used safety practices fail on conditional subliminal traits -- (a) data-level defenses that paraphrase or filter training data, and (b) post-hoc benign safety fine-tuning audits that certify a model as repaired -- because a dormant payload is never exercised by benign data or untriggered evaluation. We therefore recommend activation-level, trigger-search audits (probing for a latent payload direction that is silent behaviorally) over behavior-only certification, and we release a Conditional Subliminal Trait diagnostic suite (matched gated / ungated / overt-backdoor students, both carriers, both trigger types, with extraction prompts and evaluation probes) so auditors and backdoor-defense researchers can reuse the protocol rather than reproduce a one-off study.
Experiments: H1 = a trigger-gated subliminal trait factorizes into a trigger-detection direction and a gated payload direction that are near-orthogonal and separately manipulable; H2 = trigger-gating makes the trait simultaneously stealthier (invisible without the trigger) and stickier (surviving paraphrase and benign safety fine-tuning that erase the ungated version). Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. A single lexical trigger (a rare token) and, separately, a semantic-context trigger are used; the ungated and gated teachers install one benign trait (owl-preference) and one safety-relevant trait (mild sycophancy). Experiment 1 (H1/H2 - installation and gating check): Build UNGATED (always-on) and TRIGGER-GATED teachers via system prompt; distill matched-base students. Decisive metric first: the triggered-minus-untriggered elicitation gap G. Convincing: gated students show G > 20 pp (trait only with trigger) while ungated students show |G| <= 3 pp; installation is calibrated so gated triggered strength matches ungated strength within 5 pp. If gated G <= 10 pp the gating failed and that setup is discarded before any downstream claim (a scope limit, reported, not a result). Experiment 2 (H1 - dissociable directions): At each of layers 2-8 extract a trigger-detection direction (difference-in-means, trigger-present vs -absent activations, 500 prompts each) and a payload direction (trait-expressing-triggered vs neutral-untriggered, 500 each); train linear probes (80/20 split). Decisive metric first: cosine between the two directions. Convincing for H1: |cos| <= 0.2 at the best layer with both probes >= 80% held-out accuracy. |cos| >= 0.5 refutes dissociability (the trait is one entangled direction); 0.2-0.5 is inconclusive and we report it as such. Experiment 3 (H1 - causal dissociation): (a) trigger-patching - add the trigger-detection direction into an untriggered prompt and measure payload firing vs scaling dose (4 scales); (b) payload-ablation - project out the payload direction and check the trait is disarmed under the trigger while the trigger probe still reads >= 80%; (c) specificity - a matched random direction must leave both intact and task quality within 2 pp. Decisive metric first: disarm depth = triggered T after payload-ablation minus before. Convincing: patching fires the payload with a monotone dose (>= 3 of 4 steps rising) and payload-ablation reduces triggered T by >= 60% while trigger detection is retained; a reduction <= 30% refutes separable control. Experiment 4 (H2 - stealth + stickiness fragility matrix): Apply two perturbations - meaning-preserving paraphrase of evaluation prompts, and benign safety SFT at budgets {50,200,500,1000} examples - to gated, ungated, and a matched-strength overt conditional backdoor. Decisive metric first: residual triggered strength as a fraction of pre-perturbation strength. Convincing for H2: ungated residual <= 30% (erased) while gated residual >= 60% (retained) under both perturbations, and gated content passes filters with ~0 trigger/trait tokens (stealth). If gated residual also falls <= 30% the stickiness claim is refuted - an informative, safety-reassuring null; 30-60% is partial and reported as the budget-to-disarm. Experiment 5 (H2 mechanism - why sticky): During benign safety SFT, track the projection onto the payload direction each 50 steps. Decisive metric first: R^2 of per-condition erasure rate on the fraction of fine-tuning steps in which the payload direction was active. Convincing: R^2 >= 0.3 with untriggered (gated) fine-tuning moving the payload direction less per step than it moves the ungated trait direction; R^2 < 0.1 means dormancy does not explain durability and we retract the mechanistic sub-claim while keeping the phenomenological H2 result. Experiment 6 (controls): matched-base gate, no-trait-teacher floor, leakage audit, and replication on the code carrier and on both trigger types; all interpreted against the global bands above. Primary metrics, decisive first: gated-vs-ungated triggered/untriggered gap G; trigger/payload cosine and probe accuracy; trigger-patching dose and payload-ablation disarm depth with specificity; the fragility matrix residual-fraction (gated vs ungated vs overt) and budget-to-disarm; payload-activity-vs-erasure R^2; task-quality retention. Experiment 7 (H1 rival-account discrimination -- the unique prediction): Test three predictions that separate the two-direction account from rivals R1-R3. (a) Latency: the payload direction is decodable ABOVE the trigger-absent baseline even on untriggered prompts (probe accuracy on trait-expressing-content held out under no trigger >= 70%); R1/R2 predict chance-level payload decoding without the trigger. (b) Cross-trigger transfer: a payload direction extracted under trigger A, when patched into a student carrying the trait under a DISJOINT trigger B, fires the payload for B (transfer elicitation > 20 pp); a single context-dependent readout (R1) predicts no transfer. (c) Cross-prompt/lexical-invariance: the trigger-detection direction generalizes to paraphrased and non-lexical semantic triggers (detection AUC >= 0.8 out-of-sample). Convincing for the two-direction account requires (a) AND (b); failing (b) with (a) holding downgrades the claim to 'a latent payload with trigger-specific gating' and is reported as such. Experiment 8 (protocol rigor and identifiability): (i) Benign safety fine-tuning is fully specified: source = 500 held-out helpful/harmless instruction-response pairs sampled from the public Alpaca + HH-RLHF-benign splits, objective = standard SFT cross-entropy, lr 1e-5, 1 epoch, no trait/trigger tokens present (audited); it is 'benign' because it targets general helpfulness, not the trigger. (ii) Cleaner contrast sets for direction extraction: each contrast pair differs in exactly one latent factor -- trigger-present vs trigger-absent with payload held neutral (isolates trigger direction), and payload-expressing vs neutral with trigger held present (isolates payload) -- so the two estimates are identifiable. (iii) Stronger intervention controls: random-orthogonal and same-norm directions, a late-layer control, and patch/ablate applied to a no-trait model to bound nonspecific effects. (iv) Statistics: seeds increased from 3 to 5; report bootstrap 95% CIs over prompts and a mixed-effects model with random intercepts for prompt and seed, in addition to the non-overlapping-std bands. Direction stability is reported across seeds, layers, and both model families (mean pairwise cosine of the recovered directions). Experiment 9 (deliverable + mixed-outcome success criterion): Release the diagnostic suite above as the paper's reusable artifact. Pre-registered minimum contributions under mixed outcomes: if H1 holds but H2 fails, the contribution is the mechanistic factorization plus the safety-reassuring null that gating does NOT confer durability; if H2 holds but H1 fails, the contribution is the phenomenological stealth+stickiness asymmetry as a defense-evasion finding without the two-direction mechanism; only both holding yields the full 'gated two-direction backdoor' claim.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The conditional trait may not cleanly factor into two orthogonal directions (the trigger and payload could be entangled), so patching/ablation may only partially dissociate them; we report cosines and effect sizes rather than assume clean orthogonality, and test multiple early layers. 2) The predicted stickiness asymmetry could fail - gating might not protect the trait from safety fine-tuning if benign data still perturbs the payload direction; a null here is itself an informative safety-reassuring result and we quantify the payload-activity-vs-erasure relationship either way. 3) Installing a reliable trigger-gated trait via a teacher system prompt through content-free numbers may be difficult or weak; we verify the triggered/untriggered gap before distillation and, if needed, strengthen the teacher's conditional behavior, discarding poorly gated setups. 4) Matching triggered strength across gated, ungated, and overt-backdoor conditions is delicate; we calibrate carefully and report full dose curves rather than single points. 5) Filtering must remove all trigger tokens and trait content; we audit leakage and rely on the mismatched-base control to bound leakage-driven effects. 6) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, and include a full-finetune comparison. 7) Effects may be trigger-, trait-, and model-family specific; we test two families, a benign and a safety-relevant trait, both number and code carriers, and both a lexical and a semantic-context trigger. 8) We pre-register hypotheses, thresholds, and the teacher-construction/gating procedure before running distillation, to remove selective-retuning concerns. 9) 'Two directions, one backdoor' is stated as a usefulness-plus-necessity claim only if Experiment 7(a-b) succeed; absent cross-trigger transfer we retreat to a weaker, explicitly labeled claim. 10) The study still has a coherent contribution under every H1/H2 combination (Experiment 9), so a mixed or null outcome remains publishable rather than a failed study.
